newsitem.title: USA: ITT Q1 profits narrowly top expectations.
newsitem.headline: ITT Q1 profits narrowly top expectations.

text.p: ITT Corp Tuesday reported first quarter net income that exceeded Wall Street estimates.
But the gain was not as great as seen on first blush, analysts point out. They asked to not be identified.
ITT reported earnings, excluding several one-time items and assets held for disposition, of $0.27 per share.

That appeared well above the First Call consensus for the period of $0.14. But analysts say that estimate included what ITT calls assets held for disposition, which had a loss of $0.11. Earnings including the assets held for disposition were $0.16 per share.
ITT compared its earnings with $0.15 per share in 1996's initial quarter, which also excludes assets now held for disposition, which contributed earnings of $0.02 last year.
The company's stock opened up 1/2 at 58-1/2 on the news and traded at 58-5/8 before fading to 58-3/8 in late morning.

The one-time items identified by ITT were a gain of $0.90 per share on the sale of 7.5 million Alcatel Alsthom shares, $0.28 to cover the cost of restructuring the company's world headquarters and $0.10 per share for costs associated with Hilton Hotels Corp's hostile offer.
One analyst noted that once that offer was made, ITT "became a great operating company" by stressing its profitable operations.

Chief executive Rand Araskog said "We continue to focus on growing our core lodging and gaming businesses," adding "Both of these businesses are operationally strong, with Sheraton registering its best first quearter ever and Caesars World posting a solid performance despite major contstruction projects at its two largest properties."
